reviews.title: Disney classic stamped with shelf life
reviews.quote: As a result, “Fantasia/2000” is a hodgepodge of the new and the old, the thoughtful and the rote.

reviews.title: Fantasia 2000
reviews.quote: Yet the animators seem to have taken great care to recall Disney's classic style of animation: Though Fantasia 2000 is loaded with computer imagery, the flashy stuff is nicely integrated into more conventional scenery.

reviews.title: Fantasia 2000 Review
reviews.quote: But, like the original, the sequel is a curates egg, with moments of hilarity and beauty alternating with the pompous and the banal.

entries.basis: Exact film Whisper of the Heart (Yoshifumi Kondo, Japan July 15, 1995). Reports by Reelviews and Decent Films (retrospective reviews without usable original dates, so null). Sentiment describes each passage.

reviews.title: Whisper of the Heart
reviews.quote: An affecting and endearing collaboration between Miyazaki and Kondo, it weds a coming-of-age story with a flight of fancy to good effect.

reviews.title: Whisper of the Heart (1995) - Decent Films
reviews.quote: It moves and delights, not in another world or even a hidden magical corner, but amid the streets of Tokyo.

entries.basis: Exact film Puella Magi Madoka Magica the Movie Part 3: Rebellion (Japan Oct. 26, 2013), not the TV series or the first two recap films. Reports by Otaku USA (Nov. 5, 2013) and Beneath the Tangles (Dec. 13, 2013). Sentiment describes each passage.

reviews.title: Review: Madoka Magica The Movie – Rebellion – Beneath the Tangles
reviews.quote: The third Madoka Magic movie, subtitled Rebellion, pushes angst to extreme highs (or lows), as Gen Urobuchi puts his cast of cute magical girls in heartrending situations and weaves an unexpected tale that will leave viewers breathless.

reviews.title: Puella Magi Madoka Magica: Rebellion Review
reviews.quote: You know right from the start of Puella Magi Madoka Magica: Rebellion that something is terribly wrong, because everything is very, very right.

entries.basis: Exact film Violet Evergarden: Eternity and the Auto Memory Doll (Japan Sept. 6, 2019), not the TV series or the 2020 film. Reports by The Reel Bits (Dec. 5, 2019) and Beneath the Tangles (Feb. 13, 2020). Sentiment describes each passage.

reviews.title: Review: Violet Evergarden – Eternity and the Auto Memory Doll – The Reel Bits
reviews.quote: Which will suit series fans just fine: it doesn’t so much continue the story as extend the world a little bit, focusing just as much on the emotional arc between new characters Isabella and Taylor as it does on Violet and her fellow Dolls.

reviews.title: Violet Evergarden I: Eternity and the Auto Memory Doll (Review) – Beneath the Tangles
reviews.quote: It’s unfortunate, then, that the second half of the film, which focuses on Isabella’s past and future while bringing another character into the center of the account, isn’t as strong as the first.

entries.basis: Exact film The Boy and the Beast (Mamoru Hosoda, Japan July 11, 2015), not other Hosoda films. Reports by The Film Stage (March 2, 2016, US release) and The Irish Times (page dated July 2017). Sentiment describes each passage.

reviews.title: [Review] The Boy and the Beast
reviews.quote: This one action catalyzes a wholly different fork in the road to conjure themes of parenthood (biological versus adoptive), pride, love, friendship, contrition, and emotional stability in the face of so much chaos.

reviews.title: The Boy and the Beast review: An elaborate, unique cinematic talent
reviews.quote: That darkness – and a riff borrowed from Moby Dick – powers along an entirely surprising third act as Kyûta seeks out the mysterious son of Kumatetsu's chief rival.
